Approach hint: Sarrus Rule only works for 3×3 matrices — never for 4×4 or larger. It's faster than cofactor expansion for pure numeric 3×3 matrices, but cofactor expansion is safer/necessary when variables and simplification are involved.
(i) The value of a determinant is unaltered by interchanging its rows and columns.
(ii) Interchanging any two adjacent rows (or columns) changes the sign of the determinant.
(iii) If any two rows (or columns) are identical, the value of the determinant is zero.
(iv) If all elements of any row (or column) are multiplied by a constant k, then the value of the determinant is also multiplied by k.
(v) If each element of any row (or column) of a determinant is expressed as the sum of two terms, then the determinant can be expressed as the sum of two determinants:
(vi) If to the elements of any row (or column) a multiple of any other row or column is added, the value of the determinant remains unaltered.
...without changing the value. This is the most important property — it's the core trick used in almost every proof question in this exercise.
